3
Which list contains both scalar and vector quantities?
A
acceleration, momentum, velocity, weight
B
area, current, force, work
C
distance, kinetic energy, power, pressure
D
mass, temperature, time, speed

hints: Start by sorting the tricky quantities: weight and force need a direction, while work, kinetic energy, power and pressure need only magnitude.
Remember that electric current has a direction of flow in a wire but is a scalar because it adds by ordinary arithmetic and not by vector addition.
Look for the one list where force appears alongside area, current or work, giving a mixture of vector and scalar types.
walkthrough: Recall the test: a vector has both magnitude and direction, while a scalar has magnitude only.

Apply this to the quantities in the question: acceleration, momentum, velocity, weight and force are vectors, while area, current, distance, kinetic energy, power, pressure, mass, temperature, time, speed and work are scalars.
Check each list in turn: the acceleration-momentum-velocity-weight list is all vectors, and the distance-kinetic energy-power-pressure list and the mass-temperature-time-speed list are all scalars.
The remaining list contains force, which needs direction, together with area, current and work, which need magnitude only, so it contains both types. This is option B.

A.explanation: All four are vectors because acceleration, momentum, velocity and weight each need magnitude and direction.

B.explanation: Force is a vector while area, current and work are scalars, so this list mixes both types.

C.explanation: All four are scalars because distance, kinetic energy, power and pressure are fully described by magnitude alone.

D.explanation: All four are scalars because mass, temperature, time and speed have magnitude but no direction.
